context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.section: ### N05. A scope test for the categorical GAGA margin
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.text: If “faisceaux constructibles analytiques” includes arbitrary complex-analytic stratifications, take $X=\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ and a nonzero finite constant sheaf on the closed analytic graph $Z=\{w=e^z\}$, extended by zero. It is constructible for the analytic partition $Z\sqcup(X^{\mathrm{an}}\setminus Z)$, but its support is not algebraically constructible: the graph is Zariski dense and contains no nonempty Zariski open subset, whereas algebraic constructibility uses finite algebraic strata ([Stacks 03RW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RW)). This tests a broad reading of the margin and suggests recovering an algebraic-stratification convention; it does not refute an equivalence already restricted to such strata.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.section: ### N22. The divisor class comes from units and the Kummer boundary
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.text: The text makes $d\varphi$ a “section canonique” by passing from a regular equation to its class modulo units, then applies the Kummer boundary to define the finite-coefficient local class. It asserts Zariski locality and base-change compatibility when the pulled-back equation remains regular. A proof should check that the quotient, boundary and restriction maps agree, rather than replacing “admissible” base change by every square.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The principal handwritten sequence concerns derived operations, projection and Künneth, traces over finite coefficient rings, Tor bounds and the beginning of a Lefschetz–Verdier construction. It supports the README's broad SGA 4/5 placement, while the **24 reused typescript pages** also contain operator theory, ramification, relative divisors, local algebra and an axiomatic étale-topos exposition. Those typed sources are not silently assigned to Grothendieck's authorship or treated as his own conjectures.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N38. The deleted boundedness condition has mathematical consequences
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: In the inserted phrase “loc. libre de t.f., et borné,” the words “et borné” are themselves deleted, so they cannot be treated as a surviving hypothesis on this page. An infinite direct sum of contractible two-term free complexes placed in disjoint, successively negative degrees represents the zero, hence perfect, derived object, yet its identity has no finite degreewise alternating sum on that unbounded representative. Thus the literal representative-based formula needs local bounded representatives or another specified interpretation; this is a conditional scope objection, not a reason to restore the deletion or deny the intrinsic trace of the perfect object.
